text: Android: no session resume — every app start demands full re-login
relates: T-28 — T-28's login-then-redeem token stash should ride on this ticket's session-resume/startDestination rework rather than being bolted on before it.

Impl gotcha: the start-destination decision is genuinely async and can't be
computed synchronously in NavHost's startDestination. SessionStore.token is a
blocking Keystore/EncryptedSharedPreferences read and ServerConfig.serverUrl is
an async DataStore Flow. Either read the token synchronously in MainActivity
before setContent(), or add a short loading/splash destination while both
resolve. Also: LoginViewModel never prefills the server URL at init today —
onServerUrlChange() exists but nothing collects ServerConfig.serverUrl on
construction, so that prefill is net-new wiring, not just relocating a call.

Done in 605a276. Verified via the full debug unit suite + lintDebug (green):
authedStartDestination, server-URL prefill (+no-clobber), and the
ErrorInterceptor forced-logout signal (with-token 401 emits, token-less 401
does not, non-401 does not) all have unit coverage; RootViewModel clears the
session on the signal.

Not unit-testable here (no emulator; folds into T-29): (a) MainActivity's
synchronous token read + start-destination wiring — trivial glue over the
tested authedStartDestination; (b) that ShoppingListNavHost's LaunchedEffect
collector actually navigates on a live forced-logout event end-to-end.

Design note for reviewers: forced logout WIPES the local mirror (same as
explicit logout, minus the server call) to prevent a subsequent
different-account login seeing stale lists. Accepted edge: an offline dirty
edit made in the exact window before a concurrent remote token revocation is
lost. Also: if a 401 lands while no UI collector is active (background worker,
app killed) the event is dropped, but the dead token persists so the next API
interaction after relaunch re-emits and is observed — self-heals.
